name: Torst

facts.text: Torst is a level-80 creature with 100,000 health, paired with Hurika on a high ledge of the glacier; the original patrol flight is switched off.
His powerful wings stir swirling eddies of freezing air (five 'eddie' adds), and he roots and casts Cold Snap around him.
Allakhazam lists Torst at level 85 and his drops as griffon mantles; the glacier also holds griffon icewings and chicks.
Swedish torst and Old Norse thorsti mean thirst (to verify).
facts.source: Swedish and Old Norse glossaries, to verify

story:
High on the eastern ledge, where the glacier meets the sky, the great griffons of the ice keep their roost. They were there before the giants came, the iarn dwarves say, before the dragon died even; there have always been griffons on the high places of Aegir, and the griffon icewings of the glacier are the largest and coldest of them. Torst is the cock of the roost, a beast of cold feathers and a beak like a spear-point, and his name, in the island's northern tongue, means thirst.

Nobody knows what he thirsts for. The giants say blood. The wind-riders of the island, the Vind Ryttaren, who fly the lesser griffons of the cliffs, say freedom, and they have spent a generation trying to take a chick from Torst's roost to prove it, and failed every time. The hrimthursa leave him be. He is no one's servant, only a neighbour with a temper, and his ledge is high enough above the citadel that the giants rarely think of him at all.

When strangers climb to the roost, Torst comes down to meet them. His powerful wings stir the air into swirling eddies, little whirlwinds of freezing cold that break away from him and hunt on their own, five at a time, threatening to freeze anyone caught in their wake. His beak strikes hard enough to throw a man back. The ground around him snaps with cold, and he roots whoever he dislikes to the ice so that the eddies can find them. Of old he patrolled the skies of the glacier in long circles with his mate; today he keeps to his ledge, but he has lost none of his temper.

Hurika fights beside him. They are a pair the way the giants' pairs are not: not allies, not rivals, but mates, guarding a nest, with no other thought between them.
legend: Torst and Hurika come together. Torst's eddies are adds, kill or avoid them; his root sets you up for them, so root-break. Hurika throws people off the ledge. Pull them down where it's flat if you can. A 2003 raid of about 60 did it by bolt-pulling the bird down. Kill them together or one keeps going while you work on the other. The griffon mantles are the drops everybody wants. The eddies come in fives; area damage clears them fast if they're grouped. Bring cold resists for the whole raid; the ledge is cold enough without him, and the cold snap stacks with the eddies.

loremasterTopic.text: The cock of the griffon roost on the eastern ledge. His wings freeze the air into eddies that hunt on their own. The wind-riders of the island have tried for a generation to steal a chick from him.

bookPage: From the logbook of Asmund, wind-rider of the Vind Ryttaren. Seventh attempt on the glacier roost. We came at dusk from the east, three riders, low over the crater rim. The cock was on the ledge, the hen on the nest. We were within a spear's throw of the chicks when the cock rose and beat his wings once, and the air froze around Hrafn's griffon, and it fell. We pulled Hrafn out of the snow at the bottom of the glacier, alive. His griffon we did not find. Eighth attempt in the spring. I have said that before.
